thread:
alex: Heads-up — noticed a spike of 413s from the embeddings endpoint after we enabled prefetch/local-cache routing this morning. Seen it across a few customer tenants.

maya: Ugh. Any pattern? dims, batch size, payload bytes?

alex: Mostly mixed-dims batches that hit the prefetch path. The local cache returns a list of vectors and then our splitter rejoins them and pushes over the 10MB payload limit.

kevin: So prefetch is returning vectors that cause the final request body to exceed payload limits, right? Is prefetch duplicating items or changing encoding?

alex: Not duplicating per se. Example flow: client sends 64 requests in one batch, we prefetch 20 cached vectors, runtime stitches cached + new vectors into one upstream request and the size crosses 10MB. Previously without prefetch we’d split earlier.

jin: That sounds like a semantics mismatch: prefetch should not change batching semantics. We need two options: prefer-local-cache-only-if-no-split OR let prefetch return metadata and let splitter decide.

maya: Agree. Also we don't currently emit a metric for post-merge payload bytes. Hard to detect this without digging traces. We should emit embed.prefetch.post_merge_bytes and embed.request_split_count.

kevin: Proposed API change: prefetch returns an opaque handle + size hint. Then splitter can re-evaluate split boundaries. Minimal wire change: add header `X-Embed-Prefetch-Handle` and `X-Embed-Prefetch-SizeHint`.

alex: Example config snippet for local-cache policy: 
```
local_cache_policy: 
  prefer_local: false # toggle while we roll out
  require_exact_dims: true
  return_handle_only: true
```

ui-jen: Console UX: surface a small badge on the embeddings route that shows "prefetch hits / post-merge bytes" with a histogram. That way product can see if prefetch pushes people over limits.

maya: Telemetry events to add: `embed.prefetch.hit`, `embed.prefetch.miss`, `embed.prefetch.handle_created`, `embed.post_merge_bytes_buckets`. Also tag with dims and route_id.

kevin: Rollout plan: flip `return_handle_only` behind FF, canary 5% for 24h, watch `embed.413_rate` and `embed.post_merge_bytes_p95`. Then 25% -> 100% if stable.

alex: Also need a short-term mitigation: if prefetch would cause a post-merge size > limit, fallback to non-prefetch path (i.e., fetch upstream without cached vectors) or force extra splits. Prefer fallback to avoid 413s.

jin: For quotas: if we start counting bytes post-merge for billing, make sure to document distinction between client payload and internal post-merge bytes. Some billing dashboards expect client bytes only.

maya: Good catch — add `billing.bytes.client` and `billing.bytes.internal` counters. Console docs should explain difference.

kevin: I'll open an RFC with the handle API and metrics. Short PR to runtime to implement fallback (if predicted size > limit) today.

deploy-bot: canary deploy started: embed-prefetch-handle v1 -> prod-us-east-5% (ID: canary-2026-03-18-01) :rocket:

alex: Nice. Once canary lands let's watch `embed.413_rate` and `embed.prefetch.handle_created` in the next hour.

sre-bot: Alert rule suggestion: alert if `rate(embed.413_count[5m]) > 0.5` or if `embed.post_merge_bytes_p95 > 9MB` for 10min.

ui-jen: I'll mock up the console badge and a short tooltip explaining the post-merge concept. Want it small for the 3/22 release.

alex: Thanks everyone. RFC + PR links when available.

kevin: RFC: https://rfc.internal/redwood/embed-prefetch-handle (draft)

maya: PR 2467 opened against runtime, includes metric emission and fallback logic.

alex: solid — will follow up in the RFC thread for edge cases (mixed dims + heterogenous encodings).
